nfl.oneThing: Baker Mayfield is expected to start for the Buccaneers on Sunday, barring setbacks, after three weeks out with a dislocated right thumb.

headlines.title: Mayfield set to return for the Bucs, with Bucky Irving also back at practice
headlines.summary: Baker Mayfield is expected to play against the Panthers, barring setbacks, after missing three weeks with a dislocated right thumb. He was a full participant in practice on Wednesday and Thursday. He spoke publicly for the first time since the injury and said he feels 'very confident' gripping the ball. He didn't have surgery, but he says the thumb is 'strong enough to be able to play'. Running back Bucky Irving is also back at practice, while Emeka Egbuka is still out.
headlines.whyItMatters: Tampa Bay are 1–5 and sit #16 in the NFC.

headlines.title: Charbonnet returns for Seattle as Kenneth Walker leads the league in rushing
headlines.summary: The Seahawks activated Zach Charbonnet off the PUP list, eight months after his ACL surgery. He hasn't played this season, and it isn't certain he'll play against the Chiefs on Sunday night. Kenneth Walker III, now with Kansas City, leads the NFL with 665 rushing yards, and he has outrushed Seattle by himself in one fewer game. The Seahawks rank 14th in rushing with 643 yards. Rookie Jadarian Price has missed the past three weeks with a chest injury.
headlines.whyItMatters: Seattle are 3–3 and 0.5 games out of the NFC playoff spots. Kansas City are 5–0 and the AFC's No. 1 seed, so this is a real test for the Seahawks.

headlines.title: Lamar Jackson still limited in practice before the Bengals game
headlines.summary: Lamar Jackson was a limited participant at practice on Thursday, after being limited on Wednesday too. He has missed the last two games with a left ankle injury. Reporters said he was active in warm-ups and didn't appear to favour the ankle, though media weren't there for the whole session. Baltimore's new centre, Cam Jergens, was a full participant and could make his debut if he clears the concussion protocol. Bengals safety Kyle Dugger is trending toward a return.
headlines.whyItMatters: Baltimore are 4–2 and #8 in the AFC, and Cincinnati are 3–2 and #9. Their AFC North clash in Week 7 could shift both teams in the playoff picture.

headlines.title: Giants start J.J. McCarthy, their third starter this season
headlines.summary: The Giants have named J.J. McCarthy the starter over Jameis Winston for Sunday's game at Houston. It's the third different starting quarterback New York have used this season. They traded for McCarthy four weeks ago after Jaxson Dart's knee injury. He nearly led a comeback against the Saints in the fourth quarter, in a game Winston started. Offensive coordinator Matt Nagy says the coaches want to help him 'do what he does best'.
headlines.whyItMatters: The Giants are 3–2–1 and #4 in the NFC. How McCarthy goes will shape how long they stay in the playoff picture.

teamNews.title: The Raiders' defence is the main worry
teamNews.text: The Raiders lost 33–30 to the Bills in Week 6, their third straight defeat. Their defence has allowed 30 or more points in three straight games and has failed to get off the field in key second-half moments, according to Raiders.com. Yahoo Sports says the defence has fallen apart during the losing streak.

teamNews.title: Rams matchup: Stokes against Nacua
teamNews.text: Las Vegas face the Rams in Week 7, with both teams at 3–3 and 2–4 and clinging to playoff hopes. Yahoo Sports picks Eric Stokes against Puka Nacua as one of the key battles. Nacua leads the Rams in targets and receptions while Davante Adams is on injured reserve.

teamNews.text: Mike Washington Jr. wasn't on the field for the media portion of Thursday's practice, after being limited on Wednesday with foot and back injuries. Brock Bowers was in uniform and warming up. Carter Runyon and Dont'e Thornton Jr. were full participants on Wednesday.

contextCard.title: How the NFL concussion protocol works
contextCard.body: A player diagnosed with a concussion must go through the league's protocol before he can return. It includes an independent neurological consultant, and the player must be cleared before he can play again. Several players are on the injury report with concussions this week, including Baltimore's Cam Jergens and Kansas City's Jaylon Moore, so clearance will matter for both teams.

nba.oneThing: Anthony Edwards scored 45 points, and LaMelo Ball's viral 3-pointer was confirmed as a travel, as Minnesota opened 1–0 with a 131–106 win over Miami.

headlines.title: Edwards scores 45 as the Wolves beat the Heat, and LaMelo's travel is confirmed
headlines.summary: Anthony Edwards scored 45 points with nine threes and 10 rebounds in Minnesota's 131–106 win over Miami. Giannis Antetokounmpo scored 35 for the Heat. LaMelo Ball's 3-pointer broke a 39-39 tie in the second quarter and was not called as a travel. The NBA referees' union then said Ball took four steps after gathering, when the rule allows two, and confirmed it was a travel. The union posted a clip explaining the violation.
headlines.whyItMatters: Minnesota are 1–0 and first in the Western Conference.

headlines.title: Ty Jerome's 45 points lead the Grizzlies past the Jazz
headlines.summary: Ty Jerome scored 45 points with five threes and seven rebounds in Memphis's 123–103 win over Utah. Jaxson Hayes added six blocks. Keyonte George led the Jazz with 22 points, and Lauri Markkanen had 18 points and nine rebounds. Jerome's 45 points per game ties Anthony Edwards for the league lead after one game.
headlines.whyItMatters: Memphis are 1–0 and fifth in the West.

headlines.title: Sabonis's 18 rebounds aren't enough as the Kings lose to the Clippers
headlines.summary: Domantas Sabonis had 18 rebounds and eight assists in Sacramento's 121–96 loss at the Clippers. Darius Garland led Los Angeles with 30 points, and Brook Lopez had 11 rebounds. Zach LaVine scored 28 for the Kings. Sabonis's 18 rebounds per game also top the league's leaders after one game.
headlines.whyItMatters: Sacramento are 0–1 and 14th in the West. The Clippers are 1–0 and third, so the Kings start the season in a hole.

headlines.title: Trump criticises LeBron James over his anthem warm-up
headlines.summary: President Donald Trump accused LeBron James of disrespecting the United States after the 76ers star appeared to keep warming up during the national anthem before Philadelphia's season opener against the Knicks. The video shows James practising a golf swing and jump shot. Trump called James 'a TOTAL DISGRACE' in a social media post. James, 41, is in his record 24th NBA season. His representatives didn't respond to ESPN's request for comment.
headlines.whyItMatters: The story doesn't affect the standings, but it will follow James as he makes his home debut for Philadelphia against Cleveland.

teamNews.title: Spurs open with a 116–104 loss to the Thunder
teamNews.text: San Antonio are 0–1 and tied for 10th in the West. Jared McCain's three-point shooting helped Oklahoma City, and the game was physical from the start.

teamNews.title: Wembanyama's rough opener
teamNews.text: Victor Wembanyama missed his first 12 shots. Carmelo Anthony said he didn't show 'any developed skill sets', and an NBA legend has also called him out.

teamNews.title: Three-guard lineup
teamNews.text: Sports Illustrated argues the Spurs' three-guard lineup actually dominated the Thunder, even in defeat.

teamNews.title: Next up: the Rockets on Friday
teamNews.text: San Antonio play Houston next. The Rockets are 1–0 after a 128–110 win over Dallas.
